subject: Residency anchoring proposal, operational checklist and narrowing transient hops
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Residency anchoring proposal, operational checklist and narrowing transient hops

Alice —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick follow-up with the proposal and an ops checklist attached. High level: Acme asked for an "EU/US anchoring" commitment for PHI-derived vectors plus assurance around any transient cross-region processing (analytics/telemetry). We sketched three components in the attached DPA annex:

1) Region anchoring: customer data will be processed and stored primarily in US regions we designate (us-west-2 by default), with pinning keys allowing you to request EU placement for specific datasets.
2) Transient hops: limited, short-lived cross-region processing is permitted for pre-authorized use cases (burst compute, cache warm-up, telemetry aggregation). We propose a 24h default window, configurable up to 72h by enterprise addendum and logged as a transient hop in audit logs.
3) KMS and key control: customer-managed keys (BYOK) supported; KMS handoff diagram attached. If you want us to manage keys, we’ll escrow a wrapped key with audit trail.

Action items for Acme: 1) confirm whether 24h default transient window is acceptable, 2) indicate if BYOK is required or optional, 3) provide a short list of subprocessors you need checked for region guarantees.

Ben/Laura — I included an ops checklist (spreadsheet) with the implementation steps we’d run during onboarding (routing policies, pinning rules, telemetry retention). Please add anything I missed.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Privacy Programs | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_residency_anchor_proposal_v1.pdf; ops-checklist-region-anchoring.xlsx; dpa-annex-proposed-2025-07-22.docx; kms-handoff-diagram.png

From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Darren Holt <darren.holt@acmehealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring proposal, operational checklist and narrowing transient hops

Stephanie —

Appreciate the write-up. A few clarifying points from Acme's privacy & security:

• Our baseline requirement is that PHI-derived artifacts (embeddings, cached outputs tied to patient identifiers) must not leave EU or US designated regions unless explicitly authorized by us.
• For transient hops we need a clear operational trigger and automated notice; 24h default sounds reasonable if we get a real-time webhook and an audit entry per-hop.
• BYOK: we prefer customer-managed keys for production PHI. Can you confirm how KMS rotation interacts with pinning (if key rotation forces a temporary rewrap in another region)?

Also, can you identify which subprocessors perform analytics that could cause telemetry aggregation outside the pinned region? We need names and country locations.

Alice
Director, Data Privacy | Acme Health
alice.kim@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring proposal, operational checklist and narrowing transient hops

Thanks Alice — quick operational notes from infra/ops perspective:

• Triggering: transient hops are always policy-driven. We can gate hops on explicit customer flags (DPA annex), scheduled maintenance windows, or auto-burst events. We will emit a webhook to the address you provide and write a hop event to the audit log with the request id.
• 24h vs 72h: 24h default minimizes exposure. We support an enterprise addendum to extend to 72h for specific cohorts (e.g., embeddings pre-warm for a migration). Any window >24h will require a signed exception and Ops runbook (I attached the checklist).
• KMS: BYOK is supported. For key rotation we rewrap in-place; we will not export unwrapped material across regions. There is a short-lived control-plane transaction during rotation that is logged; nothing persists outside the pinned region. If Acme requires additional guarantees we can escrow a wrapped key with dual-region binding (notes in the diagram).

Laura — can you confirm staffing/SLAs needed to support 72h exception cases (on-call handoffs)?

Ben Carter
Senior Product Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: ops-checklist-region-anchoring.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring proposal, operational checklist and narrowing transient hops

Alice / Team —

Operational commitment from Redwood:

- We will provision a dedicated routing policy scoped to Acme's account that pins PHI-tagged payloads to the selected region.
- Transient hop webhooks: delivered to a customer endpoint within 30s of hop start, and a closing webhook when the hop finishes.
- Audit retention: hop events retained for 12 months by default (longer retention available as paid add-on).
- Escalation: for any hop >24h Ops will open an incident ticket and notify Acme's Security contact; for >48h we will escalate to product leadership and provide daily status.

On subprocessors: current analytics partners that touch telemetry are listed in the attached DPA annex. Short list exported here:
- LogFlow Analytics (US) — telemetry ingestion & aggregation
- TelemetryOps Ltd (IE) — metric pipeline and alerting
- EdgeCache Partners (SG) — cache-pop orchestration (only for non-PHI cache layers unless you request otherwise)

If you need us to zero out a partner (i.e., remove them entirely for Acme), we can follow the subprocessor suppression workflow in the DPA annex with a 30-day gating window for operational changes.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: dpa-annex-proposed-2025-07-22.docx; ops-checklist-region-anchoring.xlsx

From: Darren Holt <darren.holt@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Alice Kim <alice.kim@acmehealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring proposal, operational checklist and narrowing transient hops

Team —

We reviewed the attachments with our Security and Legal. We are generally comfortable with the 24h default window if the following are added to the DPA annex:

1) A webhook delivery SLA (30s) and proof of delivery logs for hop notifications.
2) Explicit list of subprocessors and their country of processing included in Annex B.
3) A prohibition on any unwrapped KMS material leaving the pinned region; short-lived control-plane ops are allowed if logged and accompanied by evidence.

We'd like Redwood to prepare a short, signed addendum that captures the 72h exception process (who signs, how Ops raises, and the incident notification cadence). If you can produce a one-page addendum and the signed DPA annex we can loop Contracts to finalize.

Please send the proposed addendum and a redline of the DPA annex. If you can get drafts to us by end-of-day Monday, we'll aim to sign the DPA annex the following week.

Thanks — Darren Holt
VP, Security & Risk | Acme Health
darren.holt@acmehealth.com
